{{Top}}
A '''local day''' was the measurement of [[Time/Legends|time]] that it took a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] to fully rotate on its axis. Most terrestrial planets that were not subjected to tidal lock or other extreme conditions usually had a local [[Standard day/Legends|day]] in the range of 18 to 36 [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]]. Satellite planets orbiting [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giants]] could have local days which were dozens of hours long.
